段落1。
Passage 1.
每次我走出一个超级英雄电影，我也有同样的感受。
Every time I walk out of a superhero movie, I feel the same way.
我感受到一种渴望，意识到生活中应该有更多的事情。
I experience a sense of longing, realizing that there should be more in life.
冒险的渴望是人类的本能。
The desire for adventure is a human one.
超级英雄电影完美地捕捉了这种渴望。
Superhero films capture this desire perfectly.
每部超级英雄电影的情节都变成了相对可预测。
The plot of each superhero film has become relatively predictable.
世界正处于危险之中。
The world is in peril.
世界需要一位英雄。
The world needs a hero.
英雄处于危险之中。
The hero is in peril.
英雄化解险情。
The hero resolves the peril.
英雄拯救世界。
The hero saves the world.
每部电影都有一个吸引人的主角，几部昂贵的爆炸，一些缓解气氛的笑话，以及无数出乎意料地精准的拳击。
Each film has an attractive lead, several expensive explosions, a few jokes to lighten the mood, and numerous punches that land unrealistically well.
尽管我们基本上知道会发生什么，我们会继续回来寻求更多。
Even though we basically know what will happen, we keep coming back for more.
我们社会的精英们已经拒绝了超级英雄電影。
The elites of our society have rejected superhero films.
他们说这些电影缺乏任何形式的艺术性。
They say the films lack any form of artistry.
这些电影被批评太过简单，但他们给了粉丝们想要的东西。
These movies are criticized as being too simple, but they give the fans what they want.
娱乐。
Entertainment.
无论以何种形式展现英雄故事永远存在于生活。
No matter the form in which they reveal themselves, hero stories will always be present in life.
这不仅仅是为了娱乐，而且受到启发。
It's not just about being entertained, but also being inspired.
有一位作者提到，女性渴望在一场伟大的冒险中扮演着不可替代的角色。
One author has mentioned that women desire to play an irreplaceable role in a great adventure.
大多数年轻女性都希望成为某件伟大、重要的事情。
Most young women want to be a part of something grand, something important.
显然，这一原则适用于男人也一样。
It seems clear that this principle applies to men as well.
所以下次你看到你最喜欢的超级英雄时电影，不仅能娱乐，还能受到启发。
So next time you see your favorite superhero film, be entertained, but also be inspired.
让你感受到的那点渴望激励你从而有所作为。
Let that small longing you feel motivate you to make a difference.
段落2。
Passage 2.
讲故事是最有力的意味着领导者必须影响、教导和激励。
Telling stories is one of the most powerful means leaders have to influence, teach, and inspire.
讲故事可以建立人与人之间的联系。
Storytelling forges connections among people.
当谈到我们的国家、我们的社区时，和我们的家人，我们本能地明白我们共同拥有的故事很重要约束力的一部分。
When it comes to our countries, our communities, and our families, we understand instinctively that the stories we hold in common are an important part of the ties that bind.
这种理解也适用于业务一个组织的故事，以及这些故事其领导人告诉，帮助巩固关系但事实陈述却不会这样做。
This understanding also holds true in the business world, where an organization's stories, and the stories its leaders tell, help solidify relationships in a way that factual statements don't.
好故事不仅仅能创造一种感觉的连接。
Good stories do more than create a sense of connection.
他们建立了熟悉度和信任度。
They build familiarity and trust.
它们让听众融入故事之中，使他们更乐于学习。
They allow the listener to enter the story, making them more open to learning.
好故事可以包含多重含义，因此以令人容易理解的方式传达复杂的想法，出奇地经济方式。
Good stories can contain multiple meanings, so they're surprisingly economical in conveying complex ideas in graspable ways.
故事比朗诵更吸引人数据点或摘要的讨论想法。
And stories are more engaging than the recital of data points or a discussion of abstract ideas.
有关职业错误的故事以及领导者学到的东西从他们那里可以学到另一条很好的学习途径。
Stories about professional mistakes and what leaders learned from them are another great avenue for learning.
因为人们对故事有如此紧密的认同，他们可以想象他们会如何行动类似情况。
Because people identify so closely with stories, they can imagine how they would have acted in similar circumstances.
他们能够以无风险的方式。
They're able to work through situations in a way that's risk-free.
领导者还有额外福利。
There are extra benefits for leaders.
通过一个简单的个人故事，他们可以传达基本价值观。
With a simple, personal story, they can convey fundamental values.
它们可以洞悉他们自己的经验和知识，表现为更加平易近人。
They can offer insight into the evolution of their own experience and knowledge, presenting themselves as more approachable.
然后他们更有可能激励其他人想要了解更多。
And then they are more likely to inspire others to want to know more.
段落3。
Passage 3.
美国是在一波又一波的浪潮中建立起来的移民，而且移民仍然在今日的美国。
The U.S. was founded by successive waves of immigrants, and immigrants are still contributing to America today.
统计数据证明了这一点。
Statistics prove it.
在财务表现的两个关键指标上，移民胜过土生土长的美国人。
On two key measures of financial performance, immigrants outperform native-born Americans.
首先，他们更有可能成为企业家。
First, they're more likely to be entrepreneurs.
从 1996 年到 2016 年，移民创办企业的数量是美国的两倍.S. 出生的个人。
From 1996 to 2016, the pace at which immigrants started businesses was double that of U .S.-born individuals.
移民不仅越来越频繁地成为企业家，他们还常常会成功。
Immigrants aren't just becoming entrepreneurs more frequently, they're often succeeding.
超过 40% 的财富 500 强企业创始人要么是移民，要么一个人的孩子。
Over 40% of Fortune 500 companies had a founder who was either an immigrant or the child of one.
衡量财务实力的另一个关键指标是债务等级。
Another key measure of financial strength is debt level.
移民在这方面也表现得更好。
Immigrants do better in this area too.
移民较少使用信用卡购买汽车，家，或者创业。
Immigrants use credit less often for purchasing cars, homes, or starting businesses.
这导致债务水平大幅下降比土生土长的美国人多。
This results in significantly lower levels of debt than native-born Americans.
例如，34% 出生在拉丁美洲报告无信用卡或分期付款貸款債務。
For example, 34% of Americans born in Latin America report no credit card or installment loan debt.
相比之下，总人口。
This can be compared to just 19% of the general population.
他们从父母那里继承来的价值观和习惯自己的祖国有助于解释部分成功的原因。
The values and habits they bring from their own homelands help explain some of the success.
发展中国家的失业率往往较高。
Unemployment tends to be higher in developing countries.
这意味着更多的人必须成为企业家。
That means more people must become entrepreneurs.
大多数发展中国家的信贷也较为稀缺。
Credit is also scarcer in most developing countries.
这意味着个人必须储蓄更多才能实现他们的目标。
This means individuals must save more in order to achieve their goals.
或者向朋友和家人借钱而不是银行。
Or they borrow money from friends and family rather than a bank.
这意味着更少的债务和更好的信用到达美国后的结果22 至 25 节基于以下经文你刚才听到了。
That means less debt and potentially better credit outcomes when they reach the U.S. Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
